title: Where to Wear? A talk in Toronto

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Look at the tiles in a school bathroom. Some spots are worn smooth, others look brand new. Every surface has a biography written by frictional contact.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's a nice line. Is that from a real talk?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's the subtitle on the opening slide of Where to Wear, which Antoine presented with Sheldon Andrews from ÉTS at GraphQuon 2025. That's the Quebec and Ontario pre-SIGGRAPH workshop, held at the University of Toronto on November 15th and 16th.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How contact over time leaves a readable history on a surface, and how you turn that into feedback for graphics and engineering. Time, contact and energy dissipation change how a surface looks and behaves. Think tool scratches, gaming materials, robot grippers.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Easy to say, hard to simulate, I'd guess.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly how the page puts it. The deck starts from the mechanics, with Archard wear and energy-based wear laws. Then it moves to a graphics pipeline: a contact mask, orthographic volumes, tangential velocity and traction, and finally integrating all that into textures.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And how would you check it's right?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The talk floats a few validation ideas, like capturing real surfaces with GelSight and interpolating from a materials atlas.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What did Antoine take away from presenting?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Reviewers asked how the wear would be validated on real garments, not only in simulation. So his lesson is to name the evaluation gap early. A talk also surfaces those questions before the work becomes a paper.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Had he been to GraphQuon before?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He'd helped with the 2024 site at ÉTS, so it felt like the same community on the other side of the drive. He says the hallway conversations mattered as much as the podium.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Where do I find the slides?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The full write-up has the pipeline diagram, a download for the deck, and some photos from Toronto.
